tagline: Twenty clubs, 38 games each, and the most-watched league on the planet.
why: The Premier League is England's top football division and the most popular sports league in the world, watched in almost every country. In Hong Kong it's the default sports small talk: people stay up for 10pm, midnight and 3am kick-offs and support a club for life, often one they picked as a kid in the 1990s or 2000s. You don't need to know tactics. Knowing which club someone supports, how that club is doing, and a few big names gets you a long way.

essentials.title: How the season works
essentials.body: It runs August to May. Each of the 20 clubs plays every other club twice, home and away: 38 games. A win is 3 points, a draw 1, a loss 0. Most points wins the title. There are no playoffs for the title.

essentials.title: Relegation makes the bottom exciting
essentials.body: The bottom three clubs drop down to the Championship (the second tier) and three clubs come up. Staying up is worth well over £100 million, so the relegation fight is as tense as the title race.

essentials.title: Europe is the other prize
essentials.body: Finishing in the top four or five gets a club into next season's Champions League, Europe's elite club competition, which brings money and prestige. Lower places can mean the Europa League or Conference League.

essentials.title: The 'Big Six'
essentials.body: Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham are the richest and most-followed clubs. Newcastle (now Saudi-owned) and Aston Villa have pushed into that group.

essentials.title: There are other trophies too
essentials.body: The FA Cup is the oldest knockout cup in the world (since 1871) and includes amateur sides. The League Cup (Carabao Cup) is the smaller domestic cup. Winning several in one season is a 'double' or 'treble'.

essentials.title: Managers and money drive everything
essentials.body: Clubs live and die by their manager (head coach) and transfer spending. Two transfer windows, summer and January, are when players are bought and sold, and the gossip around them is a sport of its own.

essentials.title: It's tribal
essentials.body: Fans support one club, often inherited, and rivalries are deep: Liverpool vs Manchester United, Arsenal vs Tottenham (the North London derby), City vs United (the Manchester derby). Asking 'who do you support?' is the universal opener.

names.name: Manchester City
names.what: Abu Dhabi-owned superclub that won four straight titles from 2021 to 2024 under Pep Guardiola. Also facing a huge case over alleged financial rule breaches.

names.name: Pep Guardiola
names.what: Man City's manager and arguably the most influential coach of his era. Known for possession football.

names.name: Liverpool
names.what: Won the 2024-25 title in Arne Slot's first season, after Jürgen Klopp left. Then spent heavily on Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak.

names.name: Mohamed Salah
names.what: Liverpool's Egyptian forward and one of the league's all-time great goalscorers.

names.name: Arsenal
names.what: Mikel Arteta's side, runners-up three seasons in a row from 2022-23 to 2024-25 and desperate for a first title since 2004.

names.name: Manchester United
names.what: England's most decorated club in the Premier League era, with 13 titles under Sir Alex Ferguson, but struggling since he retired in 2013.

names.name: Sir Alex Ferguson
names.what: Legendary Man United manager from 1986 to 2013.

names.name: Erling Haaland
names.what: Man City's Norwegian striker, a goal machine who set the single-season record of 36 goals in 2022-23.

names.name: Chelsea
names.what: Big spenders since Roman Abramovich's era; won the expanded Club World Cup in 2025.

names.name: Tottenham Hotspur
names.what: Spurs. Famous for near misses, then won the Europa League in 2025 to end a 17-year trophy drought.

names.name: Thierry Henry
names.what: Arsenal legend and star of the 2003-04 'Invincibles', who went a whole league season unbeaten.

names.name: Bukayo Saka
names.what: Arsenal's homegrown winger and England regular.

names.name: Virgil van Dijk
names.what: Liverpool captain and one of the best defenders of his generation.

names.name: Cole Palmer
names.what: Chelsea's playmaker and the league's coolest penalty taker.

timeline.event: The Premier League breaks away from the old Football League, backed by Sky TV money.
Manchester United win the treble: league, FA Cup and Champions League.
Arsenal's Invincibles go the whole season unbeaten.
Roman Abramovich buys Chelsea, starting the era of billionaire owners.
Agüero's last-second goal wins City the title: 'AGUEROOOO'.
Sir Alex Ferguson retires; United haven't won the league since.
Leicester City win the title as 5000-1 outsiders, the greatest upset in sport.
Liverpool win their first league title in 30 years under Klopp.
Man City win four titles in a row, a first in English football.
Liverpool champions in Slot's first season; Spurs win the Europa League.

now.headline: Arsenal on top
now.detail: After 10 games Arsenal lead on 27 points, five clear of surprise package Brighton.

now.headline: Brighton's flying start
now.detail: Brighton sit second on 22, helped by 5-0 wins over Crystal Palace and at Coventry.

now.headline: Maresca's City
now.detail: Enzo Maresca replaced Pep Guardiola in the summer; City are third on 21 and Haaland leads the scorers.

now.headline: Man United in trouble
now.detail: United are 18th with 8 points after 10 games, in the relegation zone.

now.headline: A summer of new managers
now.detail: Xabi Alonso took Chelsea, Andoni Iraola replaced the sacked Arne Slot at Liverpool, and Eddie Howe left Newcastle.

now.headline: City's 115 charges verdict
now.detail: Manchester City were found guilty of breaching financial rules between 2009 and 2018 and are appealing.

local.headline: Late nights are part of it
local.detail: Hong Kong is 7 or 8 hours ahead of the UK, so matches are 8pm to 4am. 'Did you stay up for the game?' is a natural opener.

local.headline: Man United and Liverpool rule
local.detail: The two most-followed clubs in Hong Kong, with Arsenal, Chelsea and City close behind. Many fans picked a team during the 1990s and 2000s TV boom.

local.headline: Jockey Club betting
local.detail: Football betting through the HKJC is legal and popular. Lots of casual fans follow matches through their bets.

local.headline: The Messi no-show
local.detail: In February 2024 Inter Miami played in Hong Kong and Lionel Messi didn't come off the bench, causing public outrage. People still bring it up.

local.headline: Where to watch
local.detail: Sports bars in Wan Chai, Lan Kwai Fong and SoHo show the big games; Now TV holds the local broadcast rights.

debates.question: Is VAR ruining football?
debates.sides: Supporters say it fixes obvious errors. Critics say it kills goal celebrations and offside lines measured in millimetres are absurd.

debates.question: Are City's titles tainted?
debates.sides: Rivals say the financial charges put an asterisk on them; City fans say they've done nothing wrong and the quality was undeniable.

debates.question: Guardiola or Ferguson: who's the greatest manager?
debates.sides: Ferguson built several great teams over 27 years; Guardiola changed how the game is played.

debates.question: Is the Premier League too rich?
debates.sides: It dominates Europe financially, which makes it exciting but means other leagues can't keep their stars.

debates.question: Should Man United fans be patient?
debates.sides: Some say a long rebuild needs time; others say a club that size can't keep finishing mid-table.

sayThis.say: It's a long season. Ask me again in March.
sayThis.why: Safe when people get excited about early results.
A classic analysis line that's usually true.

sayThis.say: Leicester in 2016 is still the greatest story in sport.
sayThis.why: Almost everyone agrees, and it's a nice neutral topic.

sayThis.say: I'd love to watch a game at Anfield one day.
sayThis.why: Liverpool's stadium atmosphere is famous, and it invites stories.

sayThis.say: The relegation fight is honestly more fun than the title race this year.
sayThis.why: Shows you watch beyond the big clubs.

avoid: Calling it soccer with British or Hong Kong fans. It's football.
Saying 'it's just a game' to someone whose team just lost.
Pretending to support a club. Fans can tell. Say you're still picking.
Mixing up Manchester United and Manchester City.
